cards.subject: Christ praying in Gethsemane, composed for the arched window. Christ kneels half-length at the right beside a large grey rock, in his rose-red tunic and blue mantle, his hands joined on the rock and his face lifted toward the upper left, where a young angel appears in a shaft of soft golden light out of the night sky, holding out a plain gold chalice to him. His face is grave and peaceful; no sweat of blood, only a pale light on his brow. Far below at the lower left, small in the shadow of the olive trees, three Apostles lie asleep wrapped in their mantles: Peter, James and John. Twisted old olive trees, a low stone wall, and beyond the Kidron valley the walls and towers of Jerusalem under a deep blue night sky with a full moon and a few stars. Nocturnal, still, devotional. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
cards.face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; a rose-red tunic and a blue mantle; eyes lifted to the angel in sorrow and surrender. The angel is clearly different from him and from St. Michael: a youthful angel with a SOFT, ROUND face, a small straight nose, wide-set dark-brown eyes, full cheeks, a gentle mouth; short dark-auburn curls; a pale rose-gold robe and white wings edged in gold, no armour. The sleeping Apostles are small, faces half hidden: Peter as in recurring-figures.md, about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; a blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle; James as on the james_greater card, chestnut hair to the jaw and a short sparse beard; John as in recurring-figures.md, beardless with wavy golden-brown hair, in green and red-orange.
cards.basis: Luke 22:41-45 (the prayer, the strengthening angel) and Matthew 26:37-40 (Peter, James and John asleep); the angel with the cup is the standard devotional composition (Giovanni Bellini, Carlo Dolci, holy cards after Hofmann). Christ from recurring-figures.md.

cards.subject: Christ alone at the pillar after the scourging, composed for the arched window, as in the devotional image of Christ at the Column. Christ stands half-length at the centre beside a short, round column of pale veined marble, his crossed wrists bound to it with a loose cord, his head bowed a little and his eyes turned toward us with patience and love. He wears a white loincloth and his rose-red tunic has slipped from his shoulders to the ground; his body is whole and serene, with only a few thin, clean red lines on the arms and shoulders, no blood running, no torn flesh. A bundle of rods lies on the floor at the foot of the column. Behind, the paved courtyard of Pilate's praetorium: a Roman arcade of warm stone, a doorway into shadow, and far off one Roman soldier in a red cloak walking away; late-morning light falls in from the left. Quiet, compassionate, never cruel. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
cards.face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; his hair falls forward past the shoulders, his face pale and gentle, eyes turned to us; bare-shouldered in a white loincloth, shown modestly at half-length. The distant soldier is tiny, seen from behind, face not visible.
cards.basis: John 19:1 and Isaiah 53:5 (read at the Good Friday liturgy); the lone Christ at the Column after the scourging, without the tormentors, follows the devotional type of Velázquez's Christ after the Flagellation and the Baroque 'Cristo alla colonna', which keeps the card reverent. Christ from recurring-figures.md.

cards.subject: Christ crowned with thorns and mocked as king, composed for the arched window. Christ sits half-length at the centre on a low stone bench, a faded scarlet soldier's cloak thrown over his shoulders over a white loincloth, a slender woven crown of green-brown thorns on his head, a plain reed held like a sceptre in his bound hands. His face is calm and majestic, the eyes lowered in meekness, the true King in mock regalia; at most two or three tiny clean drops at the brow, no streaming blood. Behind him, in the shadow of a pillared guardroom of the praetorium, two Roman soldiers stand small and half-turned away, one with a helmet and spear. A warm, low light from a high window falls on Christ alone. Dignified, never grotesque. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
cards.face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo behind the thin crown of thorns; eyes lowered, serene. The soldiers are small and secondary, in shadow, faces turned away: one broad-shouldered with a bronze helmet, one lean and bare-headed with cropped dark hair.
cards.basis: Matthew 27:27-30 and John 19:2-5 (scarlet cloak, crown of thorns, reed); composed as the seated 'Christ crowned with thorns' of devotional painting (Guido Reni, Titian's later type) with the soldiers kept small, so the card shows the kingship rather than the mockery. cards.subject: Christ carrying the Cross meets his Mother on the way to Calvary, composed for the arched window. Christ, half-length at the right, bears a heavy plain wooden cross on his right shoulder, bending under it, in his rose-red tunic (no mantle), the thin crown of thorns on his head; he turns his face toward his Mother. Our Lady, half-length at the left, in her blue mantle over a white veil and rose-red gown, reaches out both hands toward him, her face full of sorrow and love. Behind her, a little smaller, St. John supports her. Behind them a narrow stone street of Jerusalem climbing to a city gate, with the green hill of Golgotha beyond under a clouded sky; a Roman soldier's spear-point small at the edge. No blood, no fall shown; tender and grave. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
cards.face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; the crown of thorns thin, no blood; his gaze on his Mother, full of compassion. Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, the same face matured (the same woman, not a different face), a woman of about forty-eight with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head (a rose-red gown beneath); eyes on her Son in sorrow. St. John as in recurring-figures.md: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw; a green tunic and a red-orange mantle; he stands behind her, his hand at her shoulder. The three must read as clearly different: Christ bearded in rose-red under the Cross, Mary mature and veiled in blue, John beardless and golden-haired in green and red-orange.
cards.basis: John 19:17 and Luke 23:26-28; the meeting of Christ and his Mother is the Fourth Station of the Way of the Cross and the usual image of this mystery on Rosary cards. Christ, Our Lady and John from recurring-figures.md.

cards.subject: Christ on the Cross with his Mother and St. John standing beneath, composed for the arched window: the Cross itself is the centre, close and large, not distant. Christ hangs on a plain dark wooden cross with a small blank wooden titulus (no letters), in a white loincloth, his arms outstretched, his head inclined and his eyes raised to heaven as he gives up his spirit; the thin crown of thorns; the nail wounds only as small, clean dark-red marks on hands and feet, the side not yet opened, no blood running. At the foot of the Cross, half-length and smaller, Our Lady stands at the left, her hands clasped at her breast, looking up at her Son; St. John stands at the right, his hands joined, looking up. Behind, the rocky hill of Golgotha, a darkened sky of deep blue and violet with a pale eclipsed sun, and the walls of Jerusalem low on the horizon. Solemn and devotional, the Stabat Mater. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
cards.face: Christ as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about thirty-three with a LONG OVAL face narrowing gently to the chin — a high, smooth forehead, a long straight nose with a fine bridge, calm almond-shaped dark-brown eyes under level brown brows, high, softly modelled cheekbones, a quiet closed mouth; chestnut-brown hair parted in the centre and falling in soft waves past the shoulders; a short, full chestnut beard and moustache, lightly parted at the chin; a plain gold halo; the face lifted to heaven, peaceful in surrender. Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, the same face matured (the same woman, not a different face), a woman of about forty-eight with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head (a rose-red gown beneath); she stands upright, sorrowful and steadfast. St. John as in recurring-figures.md: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw; a green tunic and a red-orange mantle; he looks up at the Lord. Unlike mother_of_church (where Mary and John turn away together and the crosses are small and far off), here Christ on the Cross fills the upper centre and the two stand apart on either side of it, facing him.
cards.basis: John 19:25-27 and Luke 23:44-46; the Stabat Mater composition (Christ between Mary and John) of Western altarpieces and devotional cards. Batch 17's mother_of_church already shows Mary and John in the foreground with distant crosses, so this card puts the Cross itself in the middle, at the moment of the last words. Faces from recurring-figures.md.

cards.subject: St. Peter's first service with the faithful of Rome, composed for the arched window: daylight and a household, clearly not the golden basilica apse of the chair_peter card. St. Peter sits half-length at the left of centre on a plain, heavy wooden chair made of straight timbers, in his blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle, the two keys (one gold, one silver) resting on his knee; he leans forward with his right hand open and extended toward his listeners, teaching, a small scroll in his left. At the right, smaller and half-length, the first Roman faithful listen: the senator Pudens in a white toga with a narrow purple border, and his young daughter with a veil and a small clay oil lamp in her hands. Beside Peter a low stone basin of clear water, the reservoir where he baptised. Behind, the colonnaded garden court of a Roman villa on the Via Salaria: umbrella pines, cypresses, a red-tiled roof, and far off the walls and temples of Rome in soft winter light. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
cards.face: St. Peter as in recurring-figures.md: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; a blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle; here gentle and earnest as he teaches. The listeners are clearly different from him and from each other: Pudens, a Roman of about fifty with a SQUARE, clean-shaven face, a short straight nose, a broad firm jaw and short-cropped dark hair greying at the temples, attentive; his daughter, about sixteen, with a small HEART-SHAPED face, dark eyes and dark hair parted under a pale veil, lips parted in wonder.
cards.basis: From the earliest times Rome kept 18 January as the day Peter first sat among its faithful, and the ancient Roman Acts place 'the seat where he first sat' at the Ostrianum on the Via Salaria, by the villa of the senator Pudens where he baptised (Catholic Encyclopedia, 'Chair of Peter'). The chair is painted plain and wooden, as the relic is. Peter's face from recurring-figures.md.

cards.subject: The finding of the True Cross at Golgotha and the miracle that told it apart, composed for the arched window: not the upraised Cross of the exaltation_cross card. At the left, half-length, the aged empress St. Helena stands with her hands raised in thanksgiving. In the centre, laid on the edge of a freshly dug pit in the pale rock, the third of three rough wooden crosses is being touched to a sick woman of Jerusalem who, on a simple litter, sits up healed, her arms lifted in joy; the two other crosses lie on the earth behind, with a plain small blank board (the title, no letters) and three iron nails on a white cloth. Behind the litter the bishop Macarius, small, holds the cross-beam steady; two workmen with mattocks rest at the edge of the excavation. Background: broken masonry of the pulled-down pagan temple, the rock of Calvary, and the walls of Jerusalem in clear morning light. Joyful and reverent. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
cards.face: St. Helena as in recurring-figures.md: the empress at about seventy-eight, a LONG, dignified face narrowing to a FIRM, slightly prominent chin — a high forehead, a STRONG, STRAIGHT ROMAN NOSE running on from the line of the brow, large deep-set grey-brown eyes under thin, arched silver brows, lean cheeks with fine lines at the eyes and mouth; silver-white hair waved back from the brow and gathered in a low bun at the nape, as on her coins, under a white veil and a slender jewelled gold diadem; a white stola bordered in gold and a deep purple imperial mantle; she looks at the Cross with wonder and gratitude. The others are small and clearly different: the healed woman, about forty, with a ROUND, flushed face, dark hair loose on the pillow, a plain linen shift; the bishop Macarius, about sixty, a LEAN, NARROW face with a hooked nose and a short dark-grey pointed beard, bare-headed with a small tonsure, in a white tunic and a white pallium with dark crosses (no mitre, unlike the white-bearded mitred bishop of exaltation_cross); the workmen tanned, in short tunics, faces turned to the miracle.
cards.basis: The Pictorial Lives, after Rufinus and Paulinus, tells how Helena, 'near eighty', had the temple over Calvary pulled down, found three crosses with the nails and the title, and how Bishop Macarius identified the true one by the healing of a dying woman; its engraving shows that moment. Helena's face is new: Eusebius gives her age as about eighty, and her coins show a straight nose, a firm chin and hair drawn back to a bun with a diadem.

cards.subject: St. John unharmed in the cauldron of oil outside the Latin Gate of Rome, composed for the arched window. St. John is seen half-length rising from a great round bronze cauldron set on a low brick hearth, dressed in a plain white tunic, his hands joined in prayer and his face lifted serenely to heaven; a soft golden light from above falls on him, and the oil is calm and golden as a bath; only a few small flames lick the hearth beneath, and no steam, no burn, no pain is shown. At the left, small, two Roman executioners with a bellows and a long iron poker stop and stare in astonishment; behind them a helmeted soldier. Behind, the Porta Latina in the brick Aurelian Wall: a single stone arch between two round towers, crenellated walls, a few cypresses and a clear evening sky. Peaceful and miraculous. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
cards.face: St. John as in recurring-figures.md: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw; here in a plain white tunic, his green and red-orange mantle laid over the cauldron's rim; the ever-young, beardless John of the Western tradition, not aged to his historical ninety; eyes raised, peaceful and joyful. The executioners are small and clearly different: one burly with a SQUARE face and a black stubble beard, one young and thin with cropped fair hair; both astonished.
cards.basis: Tertullian, quoted by St. Jerome, records that John was plunged into boiling oil at Rome under Domitian and came out unhurt; the Pictorial Lives places it outside the Latin Gate in 95. John was then about ninety, and the book's own engraving shows him old and bearded, but nearly every Western image of this scene keeps the young, beardless John of the evangelist type, so he keeps the face of the john_evangelist card.

cards.subject: St. Michael appearing at the grotto of Monte Gargano to the bishop of Siponto, composed for the arched window. St. Michael stands half-length on a rocky ledge above the dark mouth of a limestone cave, in a burst of golden light, dressed exactly as on the michael_archangel card, his sword held upright in his right hand and his left hand pointing down to the grotto that he claims for his church; his shield with the red cross on his arm; no dragon, no demon. Below at the left, smaller and half-length, the bishop of Siponto kneels in a white alb and gold cope, his mitre laid on the rock beside him, his hands joined, looking up. At the cave mouth a small white bull lies quietly (the herd's bull of the legend). Background: the rugged white cliffs and holm-oak woods of Monte Gargano, and far below the blue Adriatic under a bright sky. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
cards.face: St. Michael as on the michael_archangel card and in recurring-figures.md: a radiant youthful angel with a softly OVAL face, a smooth brow, a fine straight nose, large clear blue-grey eyes under lightly arched golden brows, rosy rounded cheeks, a small firm mouth, a gently rounded chin; thick golden curls to the jaw; a gold halo; great white wings; a silver breastplate trimmed in gold over a blue skirt, a billowing red-orange mantle; here grave and gentle, commanding, not fighting. The bishop is clearly different: about sixty, a BROAD, LOW-BROWED face with heavy cheekbones, a short blunt nose, small kind dark eyes, a wide mouth; a white tonsured fringe and a short rounded white-grey beard.
cards.basis: The Pictorial Lives recalls that St. Michael, in a vision, told the bishop of Siponto to build a church in his honour on Monte Gargano; the Gargano legend (Liber de apparitione, Golden Legend) adds the bull that led the herdsmen to the cave. Michael keeps the face and armour of the michael_archangel card; the bishop's face is new.

cards.subject: The angel freeing St. Peter from Herod's prison (Acts 12:6-10), composed for the arched window. In a dark stone dungeon, St. Peter sits up half-length on a bed of straw at the right, waking, in his blue tunic, his golden-ochre mantle beside him; the iron chains are falling open from his wrists. At the left, a tall angel in a white robe, filled with light, bends toward him, one hand touching his shoulder and the other pointing to the open door; a bright white-gold light fills the cell from the angel. On either side two Roman soldiers sleep, slumped against the wall with their spears and helmets, faces hidden. Through the opened iron gate behind, a glimpse of a moonlit Jerusalem street. Wonder and quiet, no fear. No lettering anywhere; keep every figure inside the arched window.
cards.face: St. Peter as in recurring-figures.md: about sixty-five, a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes, a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back with a curly tuft at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; a blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle; half awake, astonished and trusting. The angel is clearly different from St. Michael and from the other angels of the set: a tall, youthful angel with a LONG, NARROW face, a fine slightly aquiline nose, deep-set clear grey eyes under straight dark-blond brows, a long smooth jaw, a calm closed mouth; straight ash-blond hair to the jaw; white robe and pale silver-white wings, no armour.
cards.basis: Acts 12:1-11, retold by the Pictorial Lives (the angel, the light, the chains dropping from Peter's hands, the soldiers asleep); Raphael's Liberation of St. Peter in the Vatican Stanze fixed the composition. Peter's face from recurring-figures.md.
